executive_summary: The daily lane-lint-gauge-cron.yml fails because 33% of session_coordination rows in its own 24h window (532 of 1609, measured live via lib/coordination/lane-lint-gauge.cjs's own predicates: 380 untyped_row, 5 bodyless_row, 316 empty_sender_row) violate the gauge's 10% hygiene budget, and every violating row is written by harness machinery, not a person. Per-writer attribution over that same window shows six sites account for 438 of the 532 violations (SET_IDENTITY broadcasts 162, signal_resolved notices 125, the WORKER_SIGNAL friction channel 148, periodic_liveness_flag 3) and two cheap sibling fixes (NODE_MODULES_LOCK 66, dashboard STALE_WARNING 4) bring covered violations to 508 of 532. This PRD types and/or sender-stamps those six writers through minimal, reader-safe edits (verified against every downstream consumer that branches on the fields being changed), leaving a projected residual of about 24 of 1609 rows (1.5%), comfortably under the 10% budget. A CI census test and gauge fixture make a future untyped/unstamped writer fail fast instead of silently re-breaking the cron.

functional_requirements.title: Writer census recorded as the PRD baseline table
functional_requirements.description: One census over lib/ and scripts/ of every session_coordination insert path (canonical insertCoordinationRow callers and raw .from('session_coordination').insert sites), naming for each: file:line, kind (if any), sender_session/sender_type, and whether it is exempt under LEGITIMATELY_BODYLESS_KINDS / LEGITIMATE_EMPTY_SENDER_TYPES in lib/coordination/lane-lint-gauge.cjs. Live 24h-window attribution (measured this session against the gauge's own runLaneLintGauge over its default 24h window, 1609 rows): SET_IDENTITY/coordinator/no-kind+no-sender 162; INFO/coordinator/signal_resolved (typed, sender_session null) 125; INFO/worker WORKER_SIGNAL rows keyed on payload.signal_type with no payload.kind 148 across signal_type values feedback(75) stuck(39) harness-bug(26) spec-conflict(4) need-sweep(2) prd-ambiguous(1) other(1); INFO/system NODE_MODULES_LOCK (payload has no kind; sender_type='system' already exempt) 66; STALE_WARNING/dashboard (no kind) 4; INFO/periodic-liveness-watcher periodic_liveness_flag (typed, no sender_session, no body) 3. Residual NOT in this SD's scope, named for the record: INFO/adam solomon_consult 10 and account_switch_notice 10 (Adam's own redacted advisory lane, deliberately senderless by that lane's existing design note — out of scope, candidate follow-up), adam_channel_health_probe 2 (self-checking probe, out of scope), signal_receipt 2 (explicitly owned by SD-LEO-INFRA-COORDINATOR-RECEIPTS-BROADCAST-CONSTRAINTS-001, not this SD). FR-1's six covered writers total 438 of 532 violating rows (82%); with the two sibling fixes in FR-1b/FR-1c, 508 of 532 (95%), leaving a residual union ratio of about 1.5% against the 10% budget.
acceptance_criteria: The PRD (this document) states the per-writer violation counts above as the baseline, sourced from a live run of runLaneLintGauge/computeRowViolationCounts, not the coordinator's original raw-predicate estimate.
Every writer this SD fixes is named with its exact file:line; every writer explicitly left out of scope is named with a one-line reason.

functional_requirements.title: assign-fleet-identities.cjs SET_IDENTITY rows carry sender_session and the already-registered kind literal
functional_requirements.description: scripts/assign-fleet-identities.cjs has three raw session_coordination insert sites for SET_IDENTITY broadcasts (the rebroadcast-on-drift site around line 679-691, the new-assignment site around line 784-796, and a third variant). Each currently omits both payload.kind and sender_session, and both branches of buildIdentityMessage() already populate a non-empty `body` column, so typing the kind will not create a NEW bodyless violation. Add payload.kind: 'SET_IDENTITY' (the exact uppercase literal already registered in the DRAIN_SETS/role_drain_sets seed and recognized by lib/fleet/orphan-reroute-sweep.js as a known kind; using the lowercase 'set_identity' instead would be a DIFFERENT, unrecognized literal that the reroute sweep could then re-target and steal from a live worker's inbox — verified via risk-agent finding against orphan-reroute-sweep.js:145/162). Add sender_session: the coordinator's own resolved session id (the value already available in main() via _mySessionId / resolveOwnSessionId, already in scope at every insert site) so these rows carry real provenance instead of null. Wrap the three insert calls in try/catch: routing an insert that already reaches assertValidTarget/backpressure indirectly (if ever moved to insertCoordinationRow) or that hits a transient DB error must not abort the naming loop for every other worker mid-run — catch, warn, and continue to the next worker.
acceptance_criteria: All three SET_IDENTITY insert sites in scripts/assign-fleet-identities.cjs stamp payload.kind: 'SET_IDENTITY' (exact casing) and sender_session: <coordinator session id>.
A live 24h gauge sample shows zero untyped_row or empty_sender_row violations with sender_type='coordinator' and subject starting 'Identity'.
Existing tests in tests/unit/assign-fleet-identities-*.test.js still pass; a new assertion confirms payload.kind and sender_session are present on the constructed message object.
A single insert failure (simulated DB error) logs a warning and the naming loop continues to the next worker instead of throwing.

functional_requirements.title: worker-signal.cjs stamps payload.kind='worker_signal' beside payload.signal_type, and the coordinator drain set recognizes it
functional_requirements.description: scripts/worker-signal.cjs (~line 703-737) already stamps sender_session and a real body through insertCoordinationRow — its only gauge violation is untyped_row, because it deliberately never sets payload.kind (keying on payload.signal_type instead, a two-vocabulary split documented at the top of the file). Add payload.kind: 'worker_signal' to the payload object ALONGSIDE the existing signal_type field (additive, not a replacement — nothing currently reading payload.signal_type changes). This alone would regress the friction channel: lib/fleet/worker-status.cjs classifyCoordinationRow() checks `if (kind)` first and returns inside that branch, so an unregistered 'worker_signal' kind would flip every /signal row from classification 'actionable' (via the signal_type fallback) to 'unrecognized' before ever reaching the signal_type check — confirmed live by risk-agent against worker-status.cjs:333. To prevent that regression, register 'worker_signal' as a recognized, actionable kind in the SAME PR: add it to DRAIN_SETS.coordinator in lib/fleet/worker-status.cjs (and to the corresponding role_drain_sets DB seed row, mirroring the existing pattern for other coordinator-drained kinds) so the newly-typed rows still classify as 'actionable' via the kind path, not merely via the signal_type fallback. Confirmed non-regression: lib/coordinator/dispatch.cjs's backpressure exemption (assertSendBackpressure) already keys on payload.signal_type presence, not kind absence, so it is unaffected either way.
acceptance_criteria: worker-signal.cjs's insertCoordinationRow call includes payload.kind: 'worker_signal' alongside the existing signal_type field.
'worker_signal' is added to DRAIN_SETS.coordinator in lib/fleet/worker-status.cjs and to the role_drain_sets seed for the coordinator role.

tests/unit/coordination/kind-classification.test.js (or a new sibling test) asserts a row with payload.kind='worker_signal' AND payload.signal_type set classifies as 'actionable', basis 'drain_set' or 'informational_registry' as appropriate — never 'unrecognized'.

The existing WORKER_SIGNAL backpressure-exemption test suite (tests/unit/coordinator/dispatch-send-backpressure.test.js) still passes unmodified, confirming the exemption keys on signal_type, not kind.

functional_requirements.title: stale-session-sweep.cjs signal_resolved notices carry a real sender_session without changing sender_type
functional_requirements.description: scripts/stale-session-sweep.cjs has two signal_resolved raw insert sites (~line 2161 disposition path, ~line 2265 promotion path), both already typed (payload.kind='signal_resolved') and already carrying a real body, but both hardcode sender_session: null with sender_type: 'coordinator'. The gauge's LEGITIMATE_EMPTY_SENDER_TYPES allowlist is ['sweep','system'] and does not include 'coordinator', so these are pure empty_sender_row violations. Fix by setting sender_session to a named system principal string, e.g. 'stale-session-sweep', rather than changing sender_type away from 'coordinator' — changing sender_type to 'sweep' was considered and rejected: lib/coordinator/michael-identity.cjs:248, lib/coordinator/solomon-identity.cjs:245, and scripts/coordinator-hourly-review.cjs:154 all filter on .eq('sender_type','coordinator') for role-retarget rescue logic, and retyping these rows away from 'coordinator' would silently exclude them from those readers (confirmed by risk-agent and Explore agent independently). A sender_session value alone (any non-empty string) clears isEmptySenderRow regardless of sender_type, so this is a zero-blast-radius fix. Both sites are inside a file with 11 pre-existing session-coordination-insert-classguard-lint violations; note (informational, not a scope item) that QF-20260905-934 measured the classguard CI workflow's shallow checkout means it always falls back to advisory --all mode today, so this is not a live merge blocker, but each touched line should still carry (or keep) its existing eslint-disable-next-line pragma for the classguard rule per repo convention.
acceptance_criteria: Both signal_resolved insert sites in scripts/stale-session-sweep.cjs set sender_session: 'stale-session-sweep' (or equivalent named principal) and leave sender_type: 'coordinator' unchanged.
tests/unit/coordinator/signal-resolved-disposition-path.test.js and tests/unit/coordinator/signal-resolved-promotion-path.test.js pass with an added assertion on sender_session.
A live 24h gauge sample shows zero empty_sender_row violations for payload.kind='signal_resolved'.
No behavior change to any reader filtering on sender_type='coordinator' (michael-identity.cjs, solomon-identity.cjs, coordinator-hourly-review.cjs) — those files are untouched by this SD.

functional_requirements.title: periodic-liveness-watcher.mjs OVERDUE/UNVERIFIED flags carry sender_session and a one-line body
functional_requirements.description: scripts/periodic-liveness-watcher.mjs's emitOverdueSignal (~line 421-440) and emitPersistentUnverifiedSignal (~line 454-468) both write payload.kind='periodic_liveness_flag' (already typed) with sender_type='periodic-liveness-watcher' and NO sender_session and NO body/payload.body — the only writer in this SD's scope that is genuinely bodyless as well as senderless (confirmed: readCanonicalBody finds neither a body column nor payload.body on these inserts). Add sender_session: 'periodic-liveness-watcher' (mirroring the precedent already established in lib/periodic-liveness/owner-directive-writer.mjs:45, which uses the identical literal as its sender_session for the same class of writer) and add a one-line body field naming the process and state, e.g. body: `${row.display_name || row.process_key} is ${evaluation.state === 'OVERDUE' ? 'OVERDUE' : 'UNVERIFIED for over 7 days'}${invocationNote}` for the overdue path and the equivalent for the unverified path. These rows are owner-routed once per episode and never feed the ladder digest (per the SD's own sourcing note), so no exemption-list change is needed once they carry real sender/body — they simply stop violating.
acceptance_criteria: Both emitOverdueSignal and emitPersistentUnverifiedSignal set sender_session: 'periodic-liveness-watcher' and a non-empty body.
tests/unit/periodic-liveness/watcher-emit-overdue-signal.test.js (and its UNVERIFIED sibling if present) pass with new assertions on sender_session and body.
A live 24h gauge sample shows zero bodyless_row or empty_sender_row violations for payload.kind='periodic_liveness_flag'.

functional_requirements.title: Two cheap sibling untyped-writer fixes: NODE_MODULES_LOCK and dashboard STALE_WARNING
functional_requirements.description: Two additional writers surfaced by this SD's live census contribute 70 of the 532 measured violations (66 + 4) at near-zero fix cost and zero reader risk, so they are folded into this SD rather than left as a known gap that reopens the budget question on the next measurement. (a) lib/npm-install-lock.cjs's acquireLock() insert (~line 71) has payload {lock_type, status, holder_session, locked_at} with no payload.kind; sender_type is already 'system' (exempt), so this is a pure untyped_row fix — add payload.kind: 'node_modules_lock'. Confirmed safe: lib/worktree-manager.js's own doc states the lock protocol is payload-based (matched on payload.lock_type/status), not kind-based, and findActiveLock() filters only on payload->>lock_type/status — nothing reads on kind's absence. (b) scripts/fleet-dashboard.cjs's STALE_WARNING insert (~line 1621-1628) has no payload.kind and sender_type='dashboard' (not exempt); message_type='STALE_WARNING' is already a known UNDRAINABLE_WORKER_MESSAGE_TYPES member (lib/coordinator/undrainable-message-types.cjs) sent fire-and-forget with .catch(()=>{}), so this insert deliberately bypasses insertCoordinationRow already — add payload.kind: 'stale_heartbeat_warning' and sender_session: 'fleet-dashboard' directly to the literal insert object; body is already non-empty so no bodyless risk.
acceptance_criteria: lib/npm-install-lock.cjs's lock-acquire insert carries payload.kind: 'node_modules_lock'.
scripts/fleet-dashboard.cjs's STALE_WARNING insert carries payload.kind: 'stale_heartbeat_warning' and sender_session: 'fleet-dashboard'.
A live 24h gauge sample shows zero untyped_row violations for subject='NODE_MODULES_LOCK' or message_type='STALE_WARNING'.

functional_requirements.title: Preventive exit predicates in CI: writer-census unit test and gauge fixture
functional_requirements.description: (a) A unit test asserts each of the six/eight writer call sites fixed by FR-2 through FR-6 stamps payload.kind and (sender_session OR an exempt sender_type) at construction time — implemented as a small table-driven test that imports each writer's message-building logic where it is already a pure/exported function (buildIdentityMessage, buildIdentityMessage's rebroadcast path) and, where the insert is inline (worker-signal.cjs, stale-session-sweep.cjs, periodic-liveness-watcher.mjs, npm-install-lock.cjs, fleet-dashboard.cjs), asserts against the actual insert call via existing test doubles/fixtures in each file's test suite, so a future edit that drops a stamp fails CI naming the specific writer. (b) Extend tests/unit/coordination/lane-lint-gauge.test.js (or lane-lint-budget.test.js) with a fixture window containing one clean row per fixed shape (SET_IDENTITY-typed-with-sender, worker_signal-typed, signal_resolved-with-sender, periodic_liveness_flag-with-sender-and-body, node_modules_lock-typed, stale_heartbeat_warning-typed) asserting computeRowViolationCounts returns all-zero for that fixture. (c) The daily cron's own verdict (gh run list for lane-lint-gauge-cron.yml) is read green for two consecutive weekly readings before this workstream is considered closed — an operational, not code-level, exit predicate tracked via the existing periodic_process_registry row for this cron.
acceptance_criteria: A new or extended unit test fails (naming the offending writer) if any of the six/eight fixed call sites is edited to drop its kind or sender stamp.
The gauge fixture test in FR-7(b) passes with an all-zero result over the synthetic clean-shapes window.
Two consecutive weekly gh run list reads of lane-lint-gauge-cron.yml show conclusion=success before this SD's tracked workstream is marked closed (verified post-merge, not at PLAN-TO-EXEC gate time).

functional_requirements.title: Registry entry: gauge and its exemption list in the orphan-writers registry
functional_requirements.description: Add one entry to lib/governance/orphan-writers-registry.js ORPHAN_ENTRIES documenting the lane-lint gauge itself (writer: the six/eight fixed session_coordination call sites; reader: lib/coordination/lane-lint-gauge.cjs + scripts/coordinator-lane-lint-gauge.cjs's exceedsLintBudget; predicate: the two exported exemption constants LEGITIMATELY_BODYLESS_KINDS and LEGITIMATE_EMPTY_SENDER_TYPES ARE the declared, reasoned exemption list — no new list is introduced), following the existing 'orphan-writers-triage-pass' entry's shape as a template (validateOrphanEntry's required fields: id, entry_type from ENTRY_TYPES, writer object, reader object with file/description, predicate object with description). Note for EXEC: QF-20260904-116 is an open, unclaimed quick-fix that ALSO appends entries to this same ORPHAN_ENTRIES array (a different, unrelated set of ten orphan specimens) and moves the same baseline-count assertion; rebase/merge this FR's single new entry against main immediately before merging to avoid a silent baseline-count collision, rather than assuming this SD's diff is the only pending change to that file.
acceptance_criteria: lib/governance/orphan-writers-registry.js ORPHAN_ENTRIES gains one new, valid entry (passes validateOrphanEntry) describing the lane-lint gauge's writer/reader/predicate.
The existing orphan-writers-registry baseline-count test is updated to the new total, with a comment naming this SD as the cause of the increment.
EXEC verifies at merge time (not at PRD-authoring time) that the array addition does not collide with QF-20260904-116 if that quick-fix has landed first.
